I got past the USB 3.0 driver issues with Ryzen, without the PS/2 option. The motherboard (Gigabyte Aorus Ultra Gaming) doesn't have a PS/2 port, and while it has USB 2.0 ports it's still controlled by the USB 3.0 root controller, hence why your Windows install couldn't recognize your 2.0 ports, elitch2.

Basically what I had to do was to slipstream the drivers into the boot.wim and install.wim images, and automate the entire install process. I also could only use the blue USB ports (for my motherboard, not sure about the others).

Here are the resources I've used to help me understand how to slipstream the drivers, and automate the install process (Read through the links in the order posted):

  • http://codeabitwiser.com/2014/03/how-to-install-windows-7-with-only-usb-3-0-ports/

  • http://thecramers.us/windows/creating-a-fully-automated-windows-7-answer-file/

  • https://superuser.com/questions/715368/how-to-bypass-the-os-edition-selection-page-in-a-windows-unattended-setup

  • https://geekdudes.wordpress.com/2015/10/30/unattended-install-windows-10-using-windows-deployement-service-on-win-server-2012-r2/

  • https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/customize/desktop/wsim/add-a-device-driver-path-to-an-answer-file

  • https://social.technet.microsoft.com/Forums/ie/en-US/3a5a348c-301e-4d50-a9a2-edc3c8906f39/adding-drivers-to-windows-7-image-with-dism?forum=w7itproinstall

  • http://blog.nicholasrogoff.com/2010/09/01/how-to-bulk-unblock-files-in-windows-7-or-server-2008/

Also look up your motherboard manufacturer, they may have tools to help automatically slipstream the 3.0 drivers for you. The Gigabyte tool didn't work for me so I used the methods previously mentioned.
